result.summary: The page is largely well-structured, but the promotional banner has a serious contrast problem: white headline and body text sit on a very pale green background, making the offer details nearly unreadable. A couple of smaller consistency/imagery issues were also noted in the restaurant cards.

issues.description: In the '3 free deliveries for you' promo banner, the white headline and the white subtext ('Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10') are placed on a very light mint-green background. The contrast ratio is far below WCAG minimums, so the offer text and promo code are effectively illegible.
issues.suggestion: Use dark text (e.g., the dark green/near-black used elsewhere) on the light banner, or darken/saturate the banner background so white text achieves at least 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for the large headline).

issues.description: The 'Green Bowl Poké' thumbnail in 'Fastest near you' renders as a few flat red/green blobs on a plate, looking like a low-fidelity or placeholder asset compared with the more finished burger and ramen illustrations used for the other restaurants.
issues.suggestion: Replace the thumbnail with a finished image/illustration consistent in style and detail with the other restaurant cards, and verify the correct asset is loading.

issues.description: Card metadata is inconsistent between sections: 'Fastest near you' cards show only a delivery fee (no rating or cuisine), while 'Popular right now' cards show rating, time, fee and cuisine. This makes the faster-options row look like it is missing data.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the card metadata (e.g., add rating and cuisine type, or a consistent secondary line) across both carousels, or intentionally label the reduced variant so it does not read as missing information.
